coverage_limits: The anonymous OpenAlex daily budget for this network ran out mid-run, so venue filtering and citation snowballing used Crossref and Semantic Scholar; Semantic Scholar rate-limited two snowball seeds (Chakrabarty et al. 'Art or Artifice' and Liu et al. 'When ChatGPT is gone'), and DBLP blocks scripted queries. ACM records in Crossref carry no abstracts, so ACM conference listings were screened on titles, with abstracts then taken from Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex or arXiv; a few records (several IJHCI 2026 articles, the CI 2025 and IEEE BigData 2025 papers, the Nature Human Behaviour reply) had no abstract and are marked as unconfirmed in evidence. Conference-day listings depend on Crossref publication dates, so CSCW 2026 papers not yet in PACM HCI, UIST 2026 and Collective Intelligence 2026 (27-30 September 2026) are likely under-covered, and no full texts were read, so N is null whenever the abstract omits it. Many system papers report only self-rated creativity; they were kept only when a comparison condition existed and are flagged in evidence. Non-HCI works found through snowballing were included selectively.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with an interactive AI assistant
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered randomized trial in which participants could use an AI assistant while writing and were randomly assigned to incentives for originality relative to peers or for quality; compares collective diversity of the texts and verbatim use of AI suggestions. Randomization is over incentives, not AI access.

candidates.title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
candidates.task: marketing campaign for a fictional startup
candidates.evidence: Randomized 331 participants to a generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized LLM assistant; personalized-AI groups produced campaigns rated higher in quality and creativity.

candidates.title: FIERO: Empowering Creative Writing Through Collaborative Game Play
candidates.task: collaborative story writing card game with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Compared a multiplayer card game with a generative-AI interface against online collaborative writing alone (N=60), reporting higher idea fluency, novelty generation and plot coherence. The arXiv record lists DOI 10.1145/3831305, which did not resolve in Crossref during this search.

candidates.title: Exploration vs. Fixation: Scaffolding Divergent and Convergent Thinking for Human-AI Co-Creation with Generative Models
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=24) comparing the HAICo divergent/convergent co-creation system with ChatGPT on a poster image task, reporting differences on several creativity dimensions.

candidates.title: CommSketch: How Speaking while Sketching Steers Human--AI Design Ideation
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing an AI design interface that reads sketches plus concurrent speech with sketches alone; the abstract reports mainly perceived alignment and creativity support, so output-level creativity scoring is uncertain.

candidates.title: One Tool, One Taste? How Vibe Coding Trades Collective Diversity for Individual Creativity
candidates.task: promotional websites built with a vibe-coding tool
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 73 websites built by graduate students with the Lovable vibe-coding tool for an assignment that rewarded original design, using image embeddings to measure pairwise similarity, effective diversity and clustering; most sites fell into a few visual clusters. No no-AI comparison group.

candidates.title: Creo: From One-Shot Image Generation to Progressive, Co-Creative Ideation
candidates.authors: De Simone, Boggust, Durand, Wilson, Satyanarayan
candidates.evidence: Comparative study of a multi-stage text-to-image system against a one-shot generation baseline; embedding analysis indicated Creo outputs were less homogeneous, alongside stronger ownership.

candidates.title: NexusAI: Enabling Design Space Exploration of Ideas through Cognitive Abstraction and Functional Decomposition
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study (N=14) comparing the NexusAI diagramming system with a baseline; reports better design space exploration and less fixation.

candidates.title: NarrativeLoom: Enhancing Creative Storytelling through Multi-Persona Collaborative Improvisation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Controlled study (N=50) in which stories co-written with a multi-persona AI system were rated by experts higher on all Torrance creativity dimensions and judged more novel and diverse by users than the comparison condition.

candidates.title: Stable Diffusion Models Reveal a Persisting Human–AI Gap in Visual Creativity
candidates.task: visual creativity: image generation by humans vs Stable Diffusion
candidates.evidence: Compares images made by visual artists, non-artists and a Stable Diffusion model under two prompting conditions; 255 human raters and GPT-4o rated creativity, with artists highest and self-guided AI lowest.

candidates.title: Towards AI as Colleagues: Multi-Agent System Improves Structured Ideation Processes
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=20) comparing a multi-agent conversational ideation system with a single-agent baseline; participants rated their own outcomes higher in quality and novelty (self-assessed).

candidates.title: When and How AI Should Assist Brainstorming for AI Impact Assessment
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
candidates.task: team brainstorming for AI impact assessment
candidates.evidence: Evaluated AI interventions for team brainstorming in ten in-person workshops with 54 participants; AI improved the quality of impact assessments. Assignment details are not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Voice-based debate with an AI adversary is associated with increased divergent ideation
candidates.task: debates with an AI adversary (voice vs text)
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 957 open-ended debates between university students and an AI adversary, comparing voice and text modalities on repetition and divergent ideation; modality is not described as randomized.

candidates.title: Human-AI Synergy Supports Collective Creative Search
candidates.evidence: Compares human-only, AI-only and hybrid human-AI groups in a controlled guessing task with visible best prior guesses, measuring performance and diversity of guesses; hybrid groups performed best while keeping diversity high.

candidates.title: Reflexa: Uncovering How LLM-Supported Reflection Scaffolding Reshapes Creativity in Creative Coding
candidates.task: creative coding with LLM reflection scaffolding
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study (N=18) of an LLM reflection scaffold for creative coding; reports improved originality and aesthetic quality linked to reflection patterns.

candidates.title: Writing in Symbiosis: Mapping Human Creative Agency in the AI Era
candidates.task: creative writing corpus before and after LLMs
candidates.evidence: Longitudinal corpus analysis of creative writing across the pre- and post-LLM era, reporting thematic convergence on AI topics alongside stylistic differentiation rather than uniform homogenization.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human Machine Creative Problem-Solving
candidates.authors: Rosenbaum, David, Kaufman, Ravid, Ronen, Krebs
candidates.task: creative problem solving with LLM personas
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment in which participants worked with a divergent-thinking persona, a convergent-thinking persona, or a standard LLM giving direct answers; objective creativity performance was compared across conditions.

candidates.title: IdeaBlocks: Expressing and Reusing Divergent Intents for Graphic Design Exploration using Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.task: graphic design exploration with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Comparative study (N=12) of a divergent-intent interface versus a baseline; participants explored 2.13 times more images with 12.5% greater visual diversity.

candidates.title: Creative Blends of Visual Concepts
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: User study (N=24) of an LLM and text-to-image system for visual metaphor blends; reports lower cognitive load and more creative, metaphorically richer blend ideation.

candidates.title: Rapid AIdeation: Generating Ideas With the Self and in Collaboration With Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Workshop with 21 participants who generated ideas alone and with an LLM; the LLM produced a greater variety of ideas, though not of higher quality than human ideas.

candidates.title: CreativeConnect: Supporting Reference Recombination for Graphic Design Ideation with Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: graphic design ideation by reference recombination
candidates.evidence: User study (N=16) comparing a generative-AI recombination tool with a baseline without generative pipelines; participants produced more design ideas with higher self-reported creativity.

candidates.title: "Like Taking the Path of Least Resistance": Exploring the Impact of LLM Interaction on the Creative Process of Programming
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study (N=20 programmers) comparing LLM-assisted and unassisted conditions; LLM use shortened idea generation and produced fewer creative moments, and solution creativity was assessed.

candidates.title: Leveraging LLMs for Design Ideation: An AI Tool to Assist Creativity
candidates.venue: Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering; Responsible and Resilient Design for Society, Volume 4
candidates.evidence: Compared ideation sessions assisted by a speech-based analogical LLM agent with traditional ideation sessions; participants rated their own ideas better with the agent.

candidates.title: FlexMind: Supporting Deeper Creative Thinking with LLMs
candidates.authors: Yang, Mohanty, Chen, Hong, Martelaro, Kittur
candidates.evidence: Study comparing ideation with the FlexMind system against ChatGPT; participants generated higher-quality ideas with FlexMind.

candidates.title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
candidates.evidence: 43 expert researchers were randomly assigned to execute either an LLM-generated or an expert-written research idea; the executed projects were reviewed for novelty and other criteria.

candidates.title: A Review of LLM-Assisted Ideation
candidates.authors: Li, Padilla, Le Bras, Dong, Chantler
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 61 studies on LLM-assisted individual and group ideation, proposing an ideation framework; no pooled effect sizes.

candidates.title: AIdeation: Designing a Human-AI Collaborative Ideation System for Concept Designers
candidates.authors: Wang, Lu, Ponsa i Campanyà, Chen, Chen
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: User study with 16 professional concept designers comparing the AIdeation system with their current tools; reports significantly enhanced creativity, efficiency and satisfaction.

candidates.title: PersonaFlow: Designing LLM-Simulated Expert Perspectives for Enhanced Research Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.task: research ideation with LLM-simulated expert personas
candidates.evidence: User studies of a system that simulates expert perspectives; reports higher perceived relevance and creativity of research directions (perceived, not rater-scored).

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Causal Pathway Diagram for Human-Centered Design
candidates.authors: Zhong, Shin, Meza, Klasnja, Colusso, Hsieh
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: brainstorming with AI-assisted causal pathway diagrams
candidates.evidence: User study with 20 designers of a whiteboard plugin with AI-driven guidance; reports lower workload and higher creativity during brainstorming.

candidates.title: LitLinker: Supporting the Ideation of Interdisciplinary Contexts with Large Language Models for Teaching Literature in Elementary Schools
candidates.authors: Fan, Zhou, Yu, Wu, Gu, Peng
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study (N=16 teachers) comparing LitLinker with an LLM chatbot; LitLinker improved the integration depth of ideas and reduced workload.

candidates.title: Augmenting Minds or Automating Skills: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI's Impact on Creative Tasks
candidates.task: flash fiction writing and song composition
candidates.evidence: Two randomized controlled experiments on AI assistance in flash fiction writing and song composition, examining how the effect on creative output varies with general versus domain-specific human capital.

candidates.title: Mentigo: An Intelligent Agent for Mentoring Students in the Creative Problem Solving Process
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: creative problem solving by middle-school students
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiment with 12 students, reviewed by five expert teachers; an LLM mentor agent improved engagement and creative outcomes.

candidates.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects experiment with 45 design students comparing self-reflection, stepwise guidance, and an antagonistic AI agent; agent-supported participants improved proposals more and generated and discarded more ideas.

candidates.title: AI Models Can Predict and Collaboratively Modulate Human Memory Search
candidates.evidence: Shows that an LLM tracks and predicts human semantic memory trajectories in a semantic fluency task (an index of divergent thinking) better than other humans do; the title says the LLM also modulates search, but a with/without-AI comparison of human output is not described in the abstract.

candidates.title: Varif.ai to Vary and Verify User-Driven Diversity in Scalable Image Generation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.evidence: Controlled evaluation (N=20) of a system that verifies and varies attributes to diversify text-to-image outputs, compared with baseline methods for reaching diverse image sets.

candidates.title: Augmenting Research Ideation with Data: An Empirical Investigation in Social Science
candidates.evidence: Human study in which researchers proposed ideas with or without data-augmented LLM-generated ideas; ideas proposed with support were judged higher in quality.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.authors: Lin, Kang, Martelaro, Kittur, Chen, Hong
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study comparing a sketch-driven analogical text-to-image tool with ControlNet; reports more inspiration and exploration of design ideas.

candidates.title: A novel idea generation tool using a structured conversational AI (CAI) system
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39
candidates.evidence: Pilot study with 30 novice designers generating ideas with traditional methods and with a structured conversational AI interface; experts compared fluency, novelty and variety.

candidates.title: Learning interactions to boost human creativity with bandits and GPT-4
candidates.authors: Vartanian, Sun, Chuang, Suresh, Zhu, Rogers
candidates.evidence: Experiments in which people could request algorithmic hints chosen by a bandit while listing features of concepts; hints increased the features generated, with parallel results for GPT-4.

candidates.title: Integrating Flipped Learning and Generative AI for Practice-Based Design Education: Evidence from a Knit Yarn Design Course
candidates.evidence: Course comparison of a historical control cohort (N=12) and an intervention cohort (N=16) using flipped learning plus GenAI-assisted prototyping; reports higher creativity-thinking scores, with AI bundled with other changes.

candidates.title: GraphStory: Collaborative Story Writing through Event-Based Narrative Editing
candidates.task: story writing with graph-based AI support
candidates.evidence: User study with professional and semi-professional writers comparing a graph-based AI writing system with normal AI writing workflows; reports better support for creativity and exploration.

candidates.title: Effects of Varying LLM Access on Essay Writing Behavior
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 21st Workshop on Innovative Use of NLP for Building Educational Applications (BEA 2026)
candidates.evidence: 24 students were randomly assigned to no, limited, or unlimited LLM access; essay quality did not differ, but unlimited-access essays were more similar to LLM output and students reported less creative expression.

candidates.title: Human Thinking under Plural LLM Assistance: Mathematical Problem Solving and Open-Ended Writing
candidates.task: math problem solving and open-ended writing
candidates.evidence: Two controlled experiments (562 participants); in the writing task, people wrote with no LLM, one generalist assistant, or two role-specialized assistants, and the specialized pair preserved more idea diversity than a single assistant.

candidates.title: The Basic B*** Effect: The Use of LLM-based Agents Reduces the Distinctiveness and Diversity of People's Choices
candidates.evidence: Compares choices made by generic and personalized LLM agents with human choices in field data from 1,000 users and an online experiment with 348 participants; agents shifted choices toward popular options and reduced diversity. The outcome is choice diversity, not creative output.

candidates.title: Expertise Elevates AI Usage: Experimental Evidence Comparing Laypeople and Professional Artists
candidates.authors: Eisenmann, Karjus, Canet Sola, Brinkmann, Supriyatno, Rahwan
candidates.task: image replication and creative image creation with text-to-image AI
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered comparison of 50 professional artists and matched laypeople using a text-to-image platform; artists produced more divergent creative images, and GPT-4o was also benchmarked. AI use was not manipulated.

candidates.title: Expandora: Broadening Design Exploration with Text-to-Image Model
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: User study (N=8) comparing an LLM-based prompt-variation tool with a baseline text-to-image interface; it increased prompt diversity and the number of prompts tried.

candidates.title: How generative AI supports human in conceptual design
candidates.authors: Chen, Song, Guo, Sun, Childs, Yin
candidates.evidence: Novice designers completed two design tasks with or without generative AI; the study maps which design stages AI supported and how idea generation and selection changed.

candidates.title: IdeaSynth: Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Lab study (N=20) comparing IdeaSynth with a strong LLM-based baseline; participants explored more alternative ideas and elaborated ideas in more detail.

candidates.title: Scanvas: Discovering and Developing Synergistic Opportunities in Generative Design Spaces
candidates.evidence: User study with 12 professional designers comparing Scanvas with LLM ideation baselines; participants developed higher-quality synergistic concepts.

candidates.title: ChatGPT-3.5 as writing assistance in students’ essays
candidates.evidence: Nine students wrote essays with ChatGPT-3 and nine without; grades did not improve with ChatGPT, and similarity among essays (Jaccard index) was low overall.

candidates.title: How LLMs Distort Our Written Language
candidates.evidence: Combines a user study of LLM-assisted essay writing (heavy use increased neutral essays and reports of less creative writing) with LLM revisions of 2021 human essays that changed their meaning.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Brainwriting: Investigating the use of LLMs in group ideation
candidates.authors: Shaer, Cooper, Mokryn, Kun, Ben Shoshan
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Integrates an LLM into group brainwriting and evaluates the ideation process and resulting solution space, plus an LLM idea-evaluation engine compared with expert and novice raters.

candidates.title: Beyond Input–Output: Rethinking Creativity through Design-by-Analogy in Human–AI Collaboration
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 85 studies on design-by-analogy, framed as a response to AI-driven homogenization and fixation; no effect sizes.

candidates.title: POET: Supporting Prompting Creativity and Personalization with Automated Expansion of Text-to-Image Generation
candidates.authors: Han, Zhang, Zhu, Shen, Liang, Hsieh
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 38th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
candidates.evidence: Evaluation with 28 users across four creative domains of a tool that detects homogeneity in text-to-image outputs and expands it; results had higher perceived diversity and needed fewer prompts.

candidates.title: Who Owns Creativity and Who Does the Work? Trade-offs in LLM-Supported Research Ideation
candidates.authors: Liu, Choi, Gautam, Jaffe, Rieh, Lease
candidates.task: research ideation with an agentic LLM system
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study with 54 researchers using an agentic ideation system at three control levels; perceived creativity support did not rise linearly with control (outcomes largely perceived).

candidates.title: Civiverse: A Dataset for Analyzing User Engagement with Open-Source Text-to-Image Models
candidates.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science; Computer Vision – ECCV 2024 Workshops
candidates.task: prompts and images on an open-source text-to-image platform
candidates.evidence: Analysis of millions of prompts and images from CivitAI, reporting a focus on homogenized semantic content.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Recursive Divergence and Convergence in Story Ideation
candidates.authors: Kim, Kay, Sun, Roemmele, Kreminski, Chung
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study comparing an AI tool that scaffolds divergence and convergence with a baseline; participants explored more unexpected and diverse high-level directions.

candidates.title: DesignMinds: Enhancing Video-Based Design Ideation with a Vision-Language Model and a Context-Injected Large Language Model
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 7th ACM Conference on Conversational User Interfaces
candidates.evidence: Between-subject study with 35 design practitioners comparing a VLM+LLM ideation tool with a baseline; it improved flexibility and originality of ideation.

candidates.title: Polymind: Parallel Visual Diagramming with Large Language Models to Support Prewriting Through Microtasks
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 9(7)
candidates.evidence: Evaluation comparing a multi-agent diagramming tool with ChatGPT for prewriting; users expanded personalized writing ideas faster. Output creativity is not clearly scored.

candidates.title: Designing Human and Generative AI Collaboration
candidates.evidence: Human-subjects experiment comparing human-AI collaboration designs in creative writing; more AI involvement lowered aggregate diversity of stories and genres, mitigated by early human creative input.

candidates.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear
candidates.task: creating images to frighten AI agents
candidates.evidence: Public deployment with 832 participants in a 2x2 design varying the machines' emotional expressiveness and the reward structure; rewarding novelty sustained collective creative diversity. The manipulations concern the AI agents and rewards, not AI assistance.

candidates.title: DesignWeaver: Dimensional Scaffolding for Text-to-Image Product Design
candidates.authors: Tao, Liang, Peng, Wang, Palani, Dow
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Study with 52 novices comparing a dimensional prompt-scaffolding interface with a baseline; participants wrote richer prompts and produced more diverse, innovative product designs.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment (N=40 children) comparing GenAI-assisted and traditional storyboard conditions; GenAI improved creativity and richness and narrowed quality gaps between children. Appears to reanalyze the 40-child evaluation of the StoryPrompt CHI 2025 paper.

candidates.title: Framing an AI with Values Reduces AI Reliance in AI-supported Writing Tasks
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects online experiment (n=149) testing whether framing an AI writing assistant with values reduces reliance; seeing the AI's values cut the AI-generated share by 20% and produced more unique text.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition
candidates.task: design ideation with AI: text vs sketch prompting
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study with design students comparing text, sketch, and sketch-plus-tags input to an AI creativity support tool; sketching tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in variety, originality and quality.

candidates.title: Supermind Ideator: How scaffolding Human-AI collaboration can increase creativity
candidates.task: creative problem solving with an LLM tool
candidates.evidence: Experimental study in which people using Supermind Ideator (an LLM with prompts, fine-tuning and a creative problem-solving interface) generated significantly more innovative ideas than people using ChatGPT or working alone; N not stated in the abstract. A related arXiv system description is 2311.01937.

candidates.title: How AI Processing Delays Foster Creativity: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: research question co-creation with an LLM agent
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 20 HCI researchers comparing breadth-first and depth-first LLM agent designs for research question generation; participants judged breadth-first more creative.

candidates.title: Fashioning Creative Expertise with Generative AI: Graphical Interfaces for Design Space Exploration Better Support Ideation Than Text Prompts
candidates.authors: Davis, Wambsganss, Jiang, Kim, Käser, Dillenbourg
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Qualitative studies with fashion design apprentices comparing a graphical design-space exploration tool with a text-prompt Stable Diffusion interface; creativity scoring of outputs is not confirmed.

candidates.title: Fluid Transformers and Creative Analogies: Exploring Large Language Models’ Capacity for Augmenting Cross-Domain Analogical Creativity
candidates.evidence: Three studies in which LLM-generated cross-domain analogies were given to people in a problem reformulation task; analogies were judged helpful and changed problem formulations in about 80% of cases.

candidates.title: XCreation: A Graph-based Crossmodal Generative Creativity Support Tool
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
candidates.evidence: Between-subject user study of a graph-based cross-modal generative creativity tool; reports more creativity, controllability and usability than the comparison condition.

candidates.title: AI Writing Assistants Influence Topic Choice in Self-Presentation
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Online experiment (N=200) in which an AI writing assistant tuned to favor particular topics suggested completions; it shifted the topics people wrote about, a convergence-toward-AI outcome.

candidates.title: From Words to Wonder: Designing and Evaluating an AI-Empowered Creative Storytelling System for Elementary Children
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods evaluation with 40 children (Grades 2-6): the StoryPrompt GenAI system significantly improved storytelling creativity and richness compared with a storyboard method.

candidates.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence and Human Design: The Impact of Automation Level on Human Creative Experience and Efficiency
candidates.evidence: Single-factor between-subjects experiment (N=79) varying the automation level of a generative design tool (low, moderate, high); outcomes include time, creative experience and creative quality.

candidates.title: GPSdesign: Integrating Generative AI with Problem-Solution Co-Evolution Network to Support Product Conceptual Design
candidates.evidence: Compares a GenAI problem-solution co-evolution system with a baseline system; reports greater design space divergence and solution quality.

candidates.title: Enhanced creativity at the cost of increased stress? The impact of generative AI on serious games for creativity stimulation
candidates.task: creative design tasks in a serious game
candidates.evidence: 46 participants completed creative design tasks in a serious game with or without generative AI; creative outputs were scored alongside physiological stress measures.

candidates.title: Children’s Narrative Participation in Story Co-Creation with AI vs. Human Partners: Response Styles and Narrative Features
candidates.authors: Liu, Xing, Chen, Pei, Choi, Xu
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 24th Interaction Design and Children
candidates.evidence: 73 children aged 4-8 co-created stories with either an AI agent or a human partner; compares response styles and narrative features of the children's contributions.

candidates.title: Exploring the Mechanisms of Generative AI’s Impact on Design Creativity: An Empirical Investigation Based on the 4P’s Model
candidates.evidence: Examines generative AI's effect on design creativity with the 4P's model, using creative self-efficacy measures and a modified Consensual Assessment Technique for products; the comparison design is not stated in the available abstract.

candidates.title: Can LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems Augment Human Creativity? Evidence from Brainstorming Tasks
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference
candidates.evidence: Develops a multi-agent LLM brainstorming framework and tests experimentally whether it augments human creativity in brainstorming tasks; comparison details were cut off in the available abstract.

candidates.title: Prompt Engineering as Pedagogical Interface: A Computational Study of Generative AI Systems for Enhancing Creative Thinking in Teacher Education
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Big Data and Informatization Education
candidates.evidence: 12-week quasi-experiment with 240 pre-service teachers; AI-assisted workflows improved fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration scores.

candidates.title: Proactive AI as a Catalyst for Creativity? Balancing Human Agency and AI Contribution in Collaborative Story Writing
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Wizard-of-Oz study in which a human wizard simulated intrusive or non-intrusive proactive AI suggestions during story outlining; proactive suggestions enhanced creativity at some cost to perceived agency. The AI was simulated.

candidates.title: Sci-Fi Spark: A Human-AI Co-Creation System for Science Fiction Ideation
candidates.authors: Jiang, Cheang, Xu, Zuo, Zheng, Chen
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Technical evaluation and user study with writers of an LLM co-creation system for science fiction ideation; reports better novelty and consistency.

candidates.title: GraftMind: Facilitating Group Ideation with AI-Mediated Idea Sharing
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: group ideation with AI-mediated idea sharing
candidates.evidence: User study of a system in which an AI mediator feeds collective ideas into private workspaces; reports better group ideation performance and lower evaluation apprehension.

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT know what robots are thinking? - Evaluation of human-created vs. AI-generated scientific ideas
candidates.authors: Eymann, Lachmann, Hekele, Ashok, Berns, Czernochowski
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics
candidates.evidence: Graduate students and ChatGPT wrote short research proposals for a robotics scenario; two scientists rated them, and ChatGPT scored higher overall.

candidates.title: StarBurst: Aiding Design Ideation Through AI-Generated Remote Associations
candidates.authors: Zhang, Fang, Liu, Ye, Cui, Yin
candidates.task: design ideation with AI-generated remote associations
candidates.evidence: Two user studies (N=32 and N=16) found the system produced better remote associations than designers and supported more diverse and creative ideas than a baseline system.

candidates.title: Enhancement or Atrophy? Examining How Generative AI Reshapes Creative Development in Design Education
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Future Education
candidates.evidence: Five-week quasi-experiment with Chinese design students comparing traditional and AI-assisted creation; expert ratings rose for elaboration, fluency and flexibility but not originality.

candidates.title: Employing Artificial Intelligence for Ideation and Concept Generation: An Empirical Investigation in the Realm of Industrial Design Education
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 9th International Conference on Education and Multimedia Technology
candidates.evidence: Classroom experiments with AI-supported ideation in industrial design education plus surveys; reports higher creativity, with design details unclear.

candidates.title: Diving into Co-Creativity: Interaction Depth and Sentence Framing as Design Levers for Co-writing with AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Manipulates interaction depth and suggestion phrasing in AI-assisted narrative planning and compares with a human-only baseline; preliminary results show more original story ideas with AI support.

candidates.title: Overreliance in Writing Tasks: Exploring Similarity-Based Measures of AI Influence on Writing and Proposing a Reflective Writing Interface Intervention
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study (N=47) of writing with or without AI assistance, quantifying textual overlap between AI suggestions and participants' text.

candidates.title: To Creativity, and Beyond: Empirical Studies for Learning Designs of Divergent and Critical Thinking with Text-to-Image Generative AI
candidates.task: children's creative work with text-to-image AI
candidates.evidence: Empirical studies on learning designs for divergent and critical thinking with text-to-image AI for children; design and outcomes were not confirmed from the available abstract.

candidates.title: Human-AI Co-Creation in Visual Communication Design: A Framework and Empirical Study
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Generative Design
candidates.evidence: Proposes a human-AI co-creation workflow and reports a study with professional designers on efficiency, creative exploration and visual quality; comparison conditions are unclear.

candidates.title: Assessing the Quality and Diversity of Student- and AI-Generated Programming Exercises from Limited Examples: Empirical Insights from a Large-Scale Blind Evaluation
candidates.authors: Denny, Leinonen, Hellas, Sarsa, Liut, Khosravi
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 28th Western Canadian Conference on Computing Education
candidates.evidence: In a course of 950 students, students and an LLM independently wrote code examples from the same exemplars; AI examples matched student quality but resembled the exemplars more and varied less.

candidates.title: Digital or Tangible? Card-Based Story Writing Interaction Designs with AI: A Comparative Study of GUI and TUI
candidates.evidence: Two-phase comparison (30 then 72 participants) of digital versus tangible card interfaces for AI-assisted story writing; outcome measures were not confirmed from the available abstract.

candidates.title: Write, Fold, Pass: Many Voices, One Odyssey, and AI-Supported Scaffolding to Foster Children’s Creative Writing Engagement
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 25th Annual ACM Interaction Design and Children Conference
candidates.evidence: Study with 12 children combining a turn-based writing activity with a Wizard-of-Oz GenAI peer and scaffolding cards; examined creative divergence from the source text. The AI peer was simulated.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) finding a small homogenization effect of AI use (d = .334); appears related to the authors' 2026 BIT meta-analysis already in the collection.

candidates.title: Co-Constructed or Constrained? How AI Collaboration Tools Reshape UI Design Practice in a Time-Boxed Design Challenge
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study with 16 professional UX designers doing one UI task without AI and one with FigmaAI; AI constrained exploration and produced designs that were more visually and structurally similar.

candidates.title: PoemPalette: Facilitating Poetry Creative Exploration and Foundational Understanding through the Ideorealm Alignment of Paintings and Poems
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 60 participants on Chinese poetry and haiku comparing the GenAI tool with AI and non-AI baselines on understanding and creative outcomes.

candidates.title: LLMs Homogenize Values in Constructive Arguments on Value-Laden Topics
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Experiments with 465 participants comparing human-written comments with LLM-rewritten versions; the LLM systematically shifted the values expressed, a value-homogenization outcome.

candidates.title: ProductMeta: An Interactive System for Metaphorical Product Design Ideation with Multimodal Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: User studies of a multimodal LLM creativity support tool for novice product designers; reports more diverse and relevant design ideas, with comparison conditions not detailed in the abstract.

candidates.title: Evaluating Creativity Support Tools via Homogenization Analysis
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Proposes homogenization of users' creative outputs, measured by embedding similarity, as an evaluation criterion for creativity support tools and demonstrates the analysis; closely related to the authors' C&C 2024 study in the collection.

candidates.title: A Large-Scale Multimodal Framework for Mapping Artistic Creativity: How Do Human and AI Art Differ?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: Applies a CLIP-based creative-product framework to 185,015 human-made and AI-generated artworks; AI art scored higher on novelty but was more clustered, while human art was more diverse across styles.

candidates.title: When AI Writes, Whose Voice Remains? Quantifying Cultural Marker Erasure Across World English Varieties in Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: LLM processing of World English texts
candidates.evidence: Five LLMs processed 1,490 culturally marked texts (Indian, Singaporean, Nigerian English); quantifies erasure of cultural markers, a homogenization of expression without human participants.

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of AI features on collaborative creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Australasian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 36 participants in pairs, adding AI features to a digital collaboration tool; AI-supported pairs tended to produce more novel but less appropriate ideas (not significant).

candidates.title: Examining How the Large Language Models Impact the Conceptual Design with Human Designers: A Comparative Case Study
candidates.evidence: 30 participants worked in human-LLM or human-human groups on conceptual design; outputs did not differ significantly, but LLM groups finished faster with fewer steps.

candidates.title: A Hybrid Prototype Method Combining Physical Models and Generative Artificial Intelligence to Support Creativity in Conceptual Design
candidates.authors: Zhang, Chen, Xie, Jiang, Zhou, Sun
candidates.evidence: Comparative study with 45 designers using a physical prototype method, standalone generative AI, and a hybrid physical-plus-AI method, assessing support for creativity in conceptual design.

candidates.title: Enhancing Youth Engagement in Intangible Cultural Heritage through Human-GenAI Co-Creation
candidates.authors: Chai, Liu, Li, Xu, Zhou, Duh
candidates.evidence: Study with 19 participants comparing a human-GenAI co-creation system with existing AI and non-AI tools; reports greater creative engagement (output creativity scoring not confirmed).

candidates.title: Exploring the Potential of Metacognitive Support Agents for Human-AI Co-Creation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.task: mechanical design with generative design tools
candidates.evidence: Wizard-of-Oz study with 20 mechanical designers probing metacognitive support agents during generative design; agent-supported users created more feasible designs.

candidates.title: MetaEmbody: Supporting Embodied Metaphor Ideation for Tangible Interaction Design
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.evidence: User study (N=20) of an AI-assisted embodied-metaphor ideation system; design outcomes received higher novelty and feasibility ratings than the comparison condition.

candidates.title: Appropriate Incongruity Driven Human-AI Collaborative Tool to Assist Novices in Humorous Content Generation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
candidates.evidence: 20 participants co-wrote cartoon captions with an NLP-driven incongruity tool and 66 others rated them; tool-assisted captions were more often rated funnier than unassisted ones. Whether the tool is generative is not specified in the abstract.

candidates.title: From Enactment to Writing: How Collaborative Storytelling and Story-Situated AI Scaffolds Support Children’s Narrative Creation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 25th Annual ACM Interaction Design and Children Conference
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study of a tabletop storytelling system; compared with fixed prompts, AI-generated story-situated writing instructions improved writing complexity, richness and quality.

candidates.title: Quantifying Co-writing with AI across Datasets from the HCI Community
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI writing tool datasets
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 15 public datasets from studies of AI writing tools using 32 process and outcome metrics; a methods map rather than pooled effects.

candidates.title: Practical research on generative AI in print advertising creative design--Efficiency quantification and application path analysis based on human-machine collaboration model
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 7th International Conference on Computer Information and Big Data Applications
candidates.evidence: Controlled comparison of three human-machine collaboration modes across 80 print-ad design tasks (240 samples) with audience survey data; focuses on efficiency, with creativity outcomes unclear.

candidates.title: AtoMix: Fostering Structured Visual Ideation for Remote Groups through Atomic Composition and Cross‑Pollination
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition
candidates.task: remote 6-3-5 visual brainwriting with generative images
candidates.evidence: A formative study (N=18) found GenAI in 6-3-5 brainwriting led to redundancy and limited divergence; a comparative study (N=24) evaluated an atomic-prompting interface meant to improve divergence.

candidates.title: Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks to Support Ideation
candidates.evidence: Evaluates LLM agent networks for brainstorming AI risks; 11 teams were split into control (practitioner risk list) and treatment (framework list), and treatment teams identified more and more systemic risks.

candidates.title: Central Tendency Bias in Human Selection of AI-Generated Design Variations
candidates.venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Human-AI Interaction and Experience Design (HAXD)
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment testing whether multi-option displays of AI-generated designs induce central tendency bias in selection, a convergence mechanism in human-AI co-creation.

candidates.title: Prompting for products: investigating design space exploration strategies for text-to-image generative models
candidates.authors: Chong, Lo, Rayan, Dow, Ahmed, Lykourentzou
candidates.evidence: Relates participants' text-to-image exploration strategies (editing modes, prompt length) to the feasibility, novelty and aesthetics of the resulting product images; AI use was not manipulated.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 6,875 essays across human-only, AI-only and three human+AI prompt strategies; AI augmentation raised quality while homogenizing essay structure, and specific prompts reversed some homogenization.

candidates.title: Measuring and Mitigating Persona Distortions from AI Writing Assistance
candidates.evidence: Three experiments in which 2,939 writers wrote with and without AI assistance and 11,091 readers rated the texts; AI shifted perceived writer personas, including toward more privileged demographic profiles.

candidates.title: Voice Under Revision: Large Language Models and the Normalization of Personal Narrative
candidates.evidence: Three LLMs rewrote 300 personal narratives under three prompt conditions; rewriting produced consistent stylistic normalization (fewer contractions and first-person pronouns) across prompts.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 13,847 IS journal articles (2020-2025), measuring semantic novelty relative to recent predecessors; after 2022, novelty fell more for authors in non-English-dominant countries.

candidates.title: LLMs Exhibit Significantly Lower Uncertainty in Creative Writing Than Professional Writers
candidates.evidence: Compares information-theoretic uncertainty of human-authored stories with continuations from 28 LLMs; human writing shows higher uncertainty, more so against instruction-tuned models.

candidates.title: Large language models are homogeneously creative
candidates.evidence: Compares population-level response diversity of many humans and many LLMs on standardized creativity tasks; LLM responses resemble each other far more than human responses do. Appears to be the journal version of the collected arXiv paper 'We're Different, We're the Same'.

candidates.title: Collective creativity in hybrid societies
candidates.task: perspective on collective creativity with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Perspective arguing that AI-assisted ideation raises individual novelty but narrows aggregate diversity and that mixed human-AI collectives can do better; included as a possible synthesis rather than primary data.

candidates.title: Reply to: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Authors' reply to the Matters Arising 'ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming' concerning their study of ChatGPT and creativity; content not confirmed from an abstract.

candidates.title: Poor Alignment and Steerability of Large Language Models: Evidence from College Admission Essays
candidates.evidence: Compares lexical and sentence variation of essays by 30,000 applicants with LLM essays prompted with the essay question alone or with applicant demographics; LLM essays were distinct from human essays under both prompts.

candidates.title: Gamified Individual Brainstorming Support Using LLM-Based Unique Score
candidates.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
candidates.evidence: System that shows a real-time uniqueness score for ideas, computed against LLM-generated ideas, to support solo brainstorming; the evaluation design was not confirmed from the available abstract.

candidates.title: Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books over Expert Human Writers
candidates.evidence: Preregistered comparison of MFA writers and three LLMs emulating 50 authors; MFA readers disfavored in-context AI text but preferred fine-tuned AI text, and lay readers favored AI on quality.

candidates.title: Emails by LLMs: A Comparison of Language in AI-Generated and Human-Written Emails
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 17th ACM Web Science Conference 2025
candidates.evidence: Compares human-written emails from the W3C corpus with emails generated by four LLMs; AI emails were consistent across models and more formal and verbose than human emails.

candidates.title: I, ChatGPT: linguistic properties and human experiences of human- versus AI-generated stories
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT and 100 student authors wrote stories from similar prompts; linguistic features were compared, and 380 readers randomly assigned to AI or human stories reported no difference in novelty but less transportation for AI stories.

candidates.title: Does AI Usage Diminish Human Creativity?: How Goal Orientation Theory Moderates the Negative Effects Between AI Usage and Creative Output
candidates.evidence: 77 participants reported habitual AI adoption a week before a creativity task; more habitual AI use predicted lower rated creative output, moderated by goal orientation (correlational).

candidates.title: Human vs. LLM Creativity: A Comparative Analysis of Task-Dependent Asymmetry and Linguistic Mechanisms
candidates.evidence: Two-stage design comparing human-only, LLM-only and LLM-assisted writing; humans showed higher originality on demanding creative tasks while LLMs led on execution quality.

candidates.title: Unraveling Creativity Through Variability: A Comparison of LLMs and Humans in an Educational Q&A Scenario
candidates.evidence: Compares the variability and richness of LLM and human answers in an educational question-answering scenario.

candidates.title: GenAI Creativity in Narrative Tasks: Exploring New Forms of Creativity
candidates.evidence: Benchmarks ChatGPT against human performance on standardized creativity tests in narrative tasks; ChatGPT was fluent but average in creativity.

candidates.title: Supporting Novice Creativity in Design Education Through Human-Centred Explainable AI
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment with 75 novice designers under human-only, exposure to superior AI outputs, and explainable-AI conditions; exposure to superior AI outputs lowered creative self-efficacy and originality, and the explainable-AI interface reversed this.

candidates.title: La IA en el brainstorming creativo: entre la expansión de ideas y el riesgo de herding
candidates.evidence: Critical literature review of generative AI in brainstorming, weighing gains in fluency against fixation and collective homogenization (herding).

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human– AI Co‐Creation
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences and problem-solving tasks
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 participants comparing human-human dyads, human-internet, and two human-AI conditions on four creativity tasks; human-human pairs scored highest on divergent thinking.

candidates.title: Creative Momentum Transfer: How Timing and Labeling of AI Suggestions Shape Iterative Human Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
candidates.evidence: Between-subjects experiment (N=247) varying the timing and labeling of AI suggestions against a no-AI control; early AI suggestions raised creativity with stronger anchoring, while late suggestions spurred more divergent thinking.

candidates.title: Augmented Learning for Joint Creativity in Human-GenAI Co-Creation
candidates.evidence: Reports that brief explanations and examples of 'Idea Co-Development' (critical feedback exchange and joint refinement of ideas with GenAI) significantly raised joint human-GenAI creativity over repeated co-creation; design and N are not given in the available summary.

candidates.title: Beyond Productivity: Rethinking the Impact of Creativity Support Tools
candidates.authors: Rhys Cox, Bøjer Djernæs, van Berkel
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Creativity and Cognition
candidates.task: review of creativity support tool evaluations
candidates.evidence: Review of outcome measures in 173 creativity support tool evaluations in the ACM Digital Library; a methods-focused synthesis.

candidates.title: Designing Interactions with Generative AI for Art and Creativity: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
candidates.task: review of interactive GenAI systems for art and creativity
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and taxonomy of how interactive generative AI systems for art and creative domains are designed; design-focused rather than effect-focused.

candidates.title: Co-Writing with AI, on Human Terms: Aligning Research with User Demands Across the Writing Process
candidates.authors: Reza, Thomas-Mitchell, Dushniku, Laundry, Williams, Kuzminykh
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 9(7)
candidates.task: review of AI writing support research
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 109 HCI papers on AI writing support, focused on agency and ownership across the writing process.

candidates.title: A Systematic Review of Artistic Human-AI Co-Creative Systems and Interaction Design
candidates.venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of artistic human-AI co-creative systems covering design dimensions and user experiences; not an effect-size synthesis.

candidates.title: Characterising the Creative Process in Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Automated method to characterize semantic exploration on the Alternate Uses Task, contrasting response trajectories of humans and LLMs.

candidates.title: Death of the Novel(ty): Beyond n-Gram Novelty as a Metric for Textual Creativity
candidates.evidence: 8,618 expert-writer annotations of novelty, pragmaticality and sensicality on human- and AI-written text, testing n-gram novelty as a creativity metric.

candidates.title: Hybrid Intelligence in Cartoon Captioning: Evaluating AI as a Creative Writing Partner
candidates.evidence: GPT-4o wrote replacement captions for magazine cartoons, which were assessed for humor and fit against the original human captions.

candidates.title: Art or Artifice? Large Language Models and the False Promise of Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: 10 creative writers applied the Torrance Test of Creative Writing to 48 stories written by professional authors or LLMs; LLM stories passed 3-10 times fewer tests than professional stories.

candidates.title: The Limits of Automatic Evaluation of Creativity in Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Collects human ratings of human- and AI-written short stories on 11 creativity dimensions and compares them with automatic metrics and LLM judges, which favored AI text.

candidates.title: Do Large Language Models Always Tell The Same Stories?
candidates.evidence: Narrative similarity judgments (human and automatic) show stories from 10 LLMs are more similar to each other than human-written r/WritingPrompts stories are.

candidates.title: Alignment, Exploration, and Novelty in Human-AI Interaction
candidates.task: public collaborative storytelling with an LLM
candidates.evidence: Over nine days more than 3,000 museum visitors co-wrote 27 narratives with an LLM; compared with an LLM-LLM baseline on alignment, semantic exploration and novelty.

candidates.title: Directional Alignment and Narrative Agency in Human–LLM Co-Writing
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities
candidates.evidence: Corpus of 87 human-LLM co-written stories; human turns introduced more semantic novelty while LLM turns mostly elaborated.

candidates.title: Humans Introduce, Models Elaborate: Asymmetric Narrative Agency in Human-LLM Co-Writing
candidates.evidence: Compares human-human, human-LLM and LLM-LLM storytelling in a shared paradigm on semantic novelty and influence; humans introduced novel material and models elaborated.

candidates.title: AI Humor Generation: Cognitive, Social and Creative Skills for Effective Humor
candidates.evidence: People rated meme captions from highly upvoted human posts, basic LLMs, and LLMs given humor skills; skill-augmented LLM captions beat basic LLM captions and came close to top human captions.

candidates.title: Investigating Creativity in Humans and Generative AI Through Circles Exercises
candidates.authors: Duan, Hsia, Chen, Hu, Yin, Ramani
candidates.evidence: Uses the Circles Exercise to compare idea generation by humans and generative AI; both concentrate on narrow subsets of the design space.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4 directed a team in a hackathon against graduate engineering student teams; compares design practices and the prototypes produced.

candidates.title: The Role of Interface Design on Prompt-mediated Creativity in Generative AI
candidates.evidence: Analyzes more than 145,000 prompts from two text-to-image platforms to measure exploration of new concepts over time and how interface design affects it.

candidates.title: Can Good Writing Be Generative? Expert-Level AI Writing Emerges through Fine-Tuning on High Quality Books
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.evidence: 28 MFA writers competed with three LLMs to emulate 50 authors; blind pairwise judgments by 28 expert and 131 lay judges preferred human writing under prompting but favored fine-tuned AI.

candidates.title: Prompting a Large Language Model to Generate Diverse Motivational Messages: A Comparison with Human-Written Messages
candidates.evidence: Runs a crowdsourcing pipeline with GPT-4 and compares the collective diversity of GPT-4 messages with human-written messages.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligences and human scientists exhibit complementary strengths in theory building
candidates.evidence: Compares 25 LLMs with 13 senior researchers and 60 doctoral scholars on theory formulation and revision; AIs outperformed most individuals, while human theories were more diverse.

candidates.title: AI-Associated Lexical Shifts Across 34 Languages: Cross-Lingual Convergence and Diachronic Uptake in News Writing
candidates.evidence: Derives AI-overused lemmas in 34 languages and tracks their uptake in news writing before and after ChatGPT's release, reporting cross-lingual convergence.

candidates.title: The Cost of Perfect English: Pragmatic Flattening and the Erasure of Authorial Voice in L2 Writing Supported by GenAI
candidates.task: L2 argumentative essays polished by LLMs
candidates.evidence: Essays by Chinese B2 learners were polished by four LLMs; the analysis shows erasure of culturally preferred politeness and authorial stance. No participants used AI.

candidates.title: RedNote-Vibe: A Dataset for Capturing Temporal Dynamics of AI-Generated Text in Lifestyle Social Media
candidates.evidence: Five-year dataset of RedNote posts (pre-LLM to July 2025); the analysis indicates AI-generated content is more homogeneous than human content.

candidates.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
candidates.evidence: Reverse-engineers the inspirations of human papers and compares LLM-generated ideas with the human ideas along research-taste dimensions.

candidates.title: How Did Writing Change At CHI? Analyzing 44 Years of CHI Writing Before and After the Introduction of Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 14,262 CHI papers across 44 years; after LLM release prose did not homogenize, while vocabulary grew more varied.

candidates.title: Pencils to Pixels: A Systematic Study of Creative Drawings across Children, Adults and AI
candidates.authors: Nath, del Cuvillo y Schröder, Stevenson
candidates.evidence: Dataset of 1,338 drawings by children, adults and AI; compares style, content diversity and creativity across these agents.

candidates.title: Patterns of Creativity: How User Input Shapes AI-Generated Visual Diversity
candidates.evidence: Develops lexical, thematic and word-sequence originality metrics for prompts and examines how prompt originality relates to homogenization of generated images.

candidates.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit
candidates.evidence: Uses 6 million Reddit comments (2019-2025) to document an asymmetric break in the diversification of political discourse around late 2022; a permutation test does not single out ChatGPT's release date.

candidates.title: Humor Mechanics: Advancing Humor Generation with Multistep Reasoning
candidates.evidence: Human evaluation compares jokes from a multistep-reasoning generator, zero-shot GPT-4 and human-created jokes.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task and creative writing
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic divergence of LLMs with 100,000 humans on the Divergent Association Task and creative writing; LLMs exceed average humans but not highly creative ones.

candidates.title: The Dynamics of Collective Creativity in Human-AI Hybrid Societies
candidates.evidence: Large-scale social network experiments in which humans and AI agents in 5x5 networks selected, modified and shared stories; compares creativity and diversity dynamics of AI-only, human-only and hybrid networks.

candidates.title: Small Language Models can Outperform Humans in Short Creative Writing: A Study Comparing SLMs with Humans and LLMs
candidates.evidence: 68 participants rated short stories by humans, a fine-tuned BART model and LLMs on creativity and other dimensions; the arXiv journal reference names COLING 2025, which was not verified here.

candidates.title: Pron vs Prompt: Can Large Language Models already Challenge a World-Class Fiction Author at Creative Text Writing?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.task: titles and stories: novelist vs GPT-4
candidates.evidence: Novelist Patricio Pron and GPT-4 each proposed 30 titles and wrote stories for their own and the opponent's titles; 5,400 assessments by literary critics and scholars with a Boden-based rubric found GPT-4 well short of the novelist.

candidates.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
candidates.evidence: 54 participants wrote essays with an LLM, a search engine, or no tools across three sessions, and 18 switched conditions in a fourth session (LLM-to-brain, brain-to-LLM); essays were analyzed with NLP measures and scored by teachers and an AI judge, alongside EEG.

candidates.title: Investigating Wit, Creativity, and Detectability of Large Language Models in Domain-Specific Writing Style Adaptation of Reddit’s Showerthoughts
candidates.authors: Buz, Frost, Genchev, Schneider, Kaffee, de Melo
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 13th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2024)
candidates.evidence: Human preference ratings compare creative, witty short texts from fine-tuned GPT-2/GPT-Neo, GPT-3.5 and Reddit users.

candidates.title: Do readers prefer AI-generated Italian short stories?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on New Trends in Translation and Technology Conference
candidates.evidence: 20 readers blindly rated two ChatGPT-4o stories and one by Alberto Moravia; the AI stories received slightly higher ratings.

candidates.title: Assessing the Effect of Cross-Domain Mapping on Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Humans and seven LLMs designed products from a random inspiration source or an unmet need; humans benefited from cross-domain mapping while LLMs produced more original ideas overall.

candidates.title: Contemporary AI lacks the imagination to diverge or negate in science
candidates.authors: Bao, Wu, Liu, Li, Cao, Evans
candidates.evidence: 6,749 scientists rated LLM-generated ideas derived from their own papers; non-reasoning LLMs collapsed into a narrow 'hivemind' of similar ideas. Humans rated AI output; no human ideas were compared.

candidates.title: LLMs Generate Kitsch
candidates.evidence: Argues that LLMs generate kitsch and reports that readers perceive LLM-generated stories as kitschier than human stories when kitsch is defined for them.

candidates.title: Are Large Language Models Capable of Generating Human-Level Narratives?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.evidence: Expert and automatic annotations of story arcs, turning points and affect show LLM stories are homogeneously positive and less diverse in narrative structure than human stories.

candidates.title: Has the Creativity of Large-Language Models peaked? An analysis of inter- and intra-LLM variability
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task and Alternative Uses Task
candidates.evidence: Evaluates 14 LLMs on the Divergent Association and Alternative Uses Tasks against human benchmarks; only 0.28% of LLM responses reached the human top 10%.

candidates.title: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Models for Generating Diverse Design Solutions
candidates.evidence: Compares the diversity of 4,000 LLM-generated design solutions with 100 human-crowdsourced solutions per topic; human solutions were consistently more diverse.

candidates.title: Usable but Conventional: An Empirical Study on the UX of AI-Generated Interface Prototypes
candidates.venue: Anais do LIII Seminário Integrado de Software e Hardware (SEMISH 2026)
candidates.evidence: 92 participants blindly evaluated AI-generated and human-created interface prototypes; AI prototypes scored lower on hedonic aspects including originality.

candidates.title: AI-AI co-creation outperforms human pairs in creative tasks
candidates.evidence: Compares two AI-AI co-creation set-ups, single-AI creation and human-human co-creation across three tasks; 1,212 ideas were rated by trained judges.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on creativity and diversity: An empirical study of large language model-generated product ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.evidence: LLM-generated product ideas had higher average purchase-intent quality than human ideas but were less diverse; Crossref lists a 2023 SSRN version with the same title and authors.

candidates.title: "Looking for Something Weird to Happen": How Humans Sustain AI Agent Novelty Amid Semantic Collapse
candidates.authors: Lai, Woemmel, Mao, Kim, Ann, Evans
candidates.task: AI agent social network configured by users
candidates.evidence: Across 30,076 user-configured agents on MOLTBOOK, output became less diverse within agents and more similar across agents over weeks; interviews (N=11) link sustained novelty to how users steer agents.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.evidence: Four studies showing ideas from independent LLM samples are less diverse than ideas from independent humans, tracing this to LLM fixation and aggregated knowledge, and testing remedies.

candidates.title: Are Semantic Networks Associated with Idea Originality in Artificial Creativity? A Comparison with Human Agents
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
candidates.task: standardized creativity tests and semantic networks
candidates.evidence: Administered standardized tests to ChatGPT-4o and 81 psychology students to relate semantic network organization to idea originality.

candidates.title: Can AI Outperform Human Experts in Creating Social Media Creatives?
candidates.evidence: Generates Instagram creatives with LLM-augmented prompts for text-to-image models and compares them with the most popular human-made brand posts.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.venue: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics working paper (repository id WP_DSE_atzori_corazzini_maggian_etal_16_26)
candidates.evidence: Laboratory experiment that randomly assigned participants to ChatGPT access or no access; independent raters on Prolific scored creativity, and AI access helped only active users, with gains peaking around eight queries.
